The diagonals of a rectangle are congruent and bisect each other, so \(BD = AC = 8\) cm and O is the midpoint of seg BD.
So \(BO = \frac{1}{2} \times 8 = 4\) cm.
In rectangle ABCD, side AD \(\parallel\) side BC and seg AC is a transversal, so \(\angle ACB\) and \(\angle CAD\) are alternate angles.
So \(\angle ACB = \angle CAD = 35^{\circ}\).
Hence \(BO = 4\) cm and \(\angle ACB = 35^{\circ}\).

All sides of a rhombus are congruent, so \(QR = PQ = 7.5\).
A rhombus is a parallelogram, so \(\angle QPS\) and \(\angle PQR\) are adjacent angles and are therefore supplementary.
So \(\angle PQR = 180^{\circ} - 75^{\circ} = 105^{\circ}\).
\(\angle SRQ\) is opposite to \(\angle QPS\), and opposite angles of a parallelogram are congruent, so \(\angle SRQ = 75^{\circ}\).
Hence \(QR = 7.5\), \(\angle PQR = 105^{\circ}\) and \(\angle SRQ = 75^{\circ}\).

The diagonals of a square are perpendicular bisectors of each other, so \(\angle IMJ = 90^{\circ}\).
Each angle of a square measures \(90^{\circ}\) and a diagonal of a square bisects the angles through which it passes.
Diagonal IK bisects \(\angle I\), so \(\angle JIK = \frac{1}{2} \times 90^{\circ} = 45^{\circ}\).
Diagonal JL bisects \(\angle J\), so \(\angle LJK = \frac{1}{2} \times 90^{\circ} = 45^{\circ}\).
Hence \(\angle IMJ = 90^{\circ}\), \(\angle JIK = 45^{\circ}\) and \(\angle LJK = 45^{\circ}\).

The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular bisectors of each other, so they cut the rhombus into four right-angled triangles whose legs are the half-diagonals.
Half-diagonals \(= \frac{20}{2} = 10\) cm and \(\frac{21}{2} = 10.5\) cm.
By Pythagoras' theorem the side \(= \sqrt{10^2 + (10.5)^2} = \sqrt{100 + 110.25} = \sqrt{210.25} = 14.5\) cm.
Perimeter \(= 4 \times 14.5 = 58\) cm.
Hence the side of the rhombus is 14.5 cm and its perimeter is 58 cm.

False.
A rhombus is a parallelogram in which all four sides are congruent, but an ordinary parallelogram only needs its opposite sides to be congruent. For example a parallelogram with sides 5 cm and 8 cm is not a rhombus.
So the statement is false.

False.
A rectangle must have all four angles equal to \(90^{\circ}\), but a rhombus only needs all four sides congruent; its angles need not be right angles. A rhombus with angles \(60^{\circ}\) and \(120^{\circ}\) is not a rectangle.
So the statement is false.

True.
Every angle of a rectangle measures \(90^{\circ}\), so both pairs of opposite angles are congruent, and by the opposite angles test the rectangle is a parallelogram.
So the statement is true.

[Textbook misprint: the book prints 'Every squre is a rectangle.' The stem is transcribed exactly as printed; read 'squre' as 'square'. Nothing in the statement or its answer turns on the spelling.]

True.
A square has all four sides congruent and all four angles equal to \(90^{\circ}\). Since every angle of a square is a right angle, it satisfies the definition of a rectangle.
So the statement is true.

True.
A rhombus is a quadrilateral with all four sides congruent, and a square has all four sides congruent, so every square satisfies the definition of a rhombus.
So the statement is true.

False.
A rectangle must have all four angles equal to \(90^{\circ}\), while the angles of a parallelogram need only be supplementary in pairs. A parallelogram with angles \(70^{\circ}\) and \(110^{\circ}\) is not a rectangle.
So the statement is false.
